sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *lo que* from B1 Unit 20 and *que* + subjunctive from B2 Unit 13. Put them after *todo* and you can say "everything that" and "everyone who". The same rule applies as always: if the group or the amount is real and you can list it, use the indicative; if it is open, use the subjunctive.

sections.title: Real or open?
rows: Todo lo que dijo es verdad.
Everything he said is true. (It was said: indicative.)
Eat as much as you want. (The amount is open: subjunctive.)
Todos los que llegaron temprano recibieron un regalo.
Everyone who arrived early received a gift. (A real group: indicative.)
Todo aquel que quiera ayudar es bienvenido.
Anyone who wants to help is welcome. (An open group: subjunctive.)

sections.title: Which one to use
sections.content: *Todo lo que* is for things and *todos los que* for people in everyday speech. *Todo aquel que* is for people and sounds more formal: you find it in rules and notices. *Cuanto*, *cuantos* and *cuantas* are a formal way to say the same: *Comparte cuanto sepas*, *Invita a cuantos amigos quieras*. You know *cuanto* from *cuanto más… más* in B1 Unit 2; here it stands for "as much as" or "as many as".

items.spanish: Todo aquel que quiera ayudar es bienvenido.
items.english: Anyone who wants to help is welcome.

items.spanish: Todos los que llegaron temprano recibieron un regalo.
items.english: Everyone who arrived early received a gift.
Invite as many friends as you like.

sections.content: English "everyone who" and "everything that" never show a mood, so ask whether the group is real. Facts and past events take the indicative; offers, rules and permissions about the future take the subjunctive.
